Explanation: To humbly negate or disagree with what someone has said.
Korean Sentence 1: 일을 다 끝내기는요. 아직 시작도 못했는데요.
English Sentence 1: I haven't finished all the work. I haven't even begun.
Korean Sentence 2: 숙제를 안 하기는요. 다 했는데 깜빡 잊고 안 가지고 왔어요.
English Sentence 2: I have done the homework. I finished it but just forgot to bring it with me.
Korean Sentence 3: 시험이 쉽기는요. 아는 것보다 모르는 것이 더 많았어요.
English Sentence 3: The test isn't easy. There were more questions I didn't know the answers to than the ones I did.
Korean Sentence 4: 한국말을 잘 하기는요. 쉬운 말밖에 못 해요.
English Sentence 4: I'm not good at Korean. I can only speak simple phrases.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 영수씨, 발표 준비는 다 했어요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 다 하기는요. 아직 시작도 못했어요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Yeongsu, are you finished preparing for your presentation?
English Sentence 5B: B: I'm not finished. I haven't even begun.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 한국말을 참 잘하시네요.
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 잘 하기는요. 아직도 모르는 게 많아요.
English Sentence 6A: A: You're so good at Korean.
English Sentence 6B: B: Not at all. There are so many things I still don't know.

Explanation: To state that something is "only" or "just" the case, with nothing more.
Korean Sentence 1: 그 사람 이름만 알 뿐이에요. 다른 것은 잘 몰라요.
English Sentence 1: I only know that person's name. I don't know anything else.
Korean Sentence 2: 건강이 좋아진 특별한 방법은 없어요. 아침마다 산책을 했을 뿐이에요.
English Sentence 2: There isn't any secret method to my health improving. All I did was take a walk every morning.
Korean Sentence 3: 고맙기는요, 시간이 있어서 조금 도왔을 뿐이에요.
English Sentence 3: No need to thank me. I just helped out because I had some time to spare.
Korean Sentence 4: 미정 씨는 같은 반 친구일 뿐이에요. 제 여자친구가 아니에요.
English Sentence 4: Mijeong is just a friend from class. She's not my girlfriend.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 영수씨, 얼굴이 안 좋아 보여요. 어디 아프세요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 괜찮아요. 좀 피곤할 뿐이에요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Yeongsu, you don't look well. Are you sick?
English Sentence 5B: B: I'm okay. I'm just tired.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 도와주셔서 감사합니다.
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 감사하기는요. 제가 해야 할 일을 했을 뿐입니다.
English Sentence 6A: A: Thank you for your help.
English Sentence 6B: B: No need for thanks. I just did what I had to do.

Explanation: To express the purpose or intent for doing something ("in order to").
Korean Sentence 1: 저는 세계 여행을 하기 위해서 외국어를 공부해요.
English Sentence 1: I am learning a foreign language in order to travel the world.
Korean Sentence 2: 저는 선생님이 되기 위해서 교육학을 전공할 거예요.
English Sentence 2: I will major in education in order to become a teacher.
Korean Sentence 3: 제 동생은 중국으로 유학을 가기 위해서 중국어를 공부하고 있어요.
English Sentence 3: My younger sibling is studying Chinese in order to study abroad in China.
Korean Sentence 4: 이튼 씨는 친구들을 위해서 고향 음식을 만들었어요.
English Sentence 4: Ethan made his hometown food for his friends.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 우디씨, 왜 그렇게 열심히 공부해요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 공무원 시험에 합격하기 위해서 열심히 공부해요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Woody, why are you studying so hard?
English Sentence 5B: B: I am studying hard in order to pass the civil service examination.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 코넨씨, 날마다 이렇게 운동하시는 거예요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 네, 저는 건강을 위해서 날마다 운동을 해요.
English Sentence 6A: A: Conan, do you exercise like this every day?
English Sentence 6B: B: Yes, I exercise every day for my health.

Explanation: To describe something in relative terms, avoiding a definitive statement ("to be on the relatively... side").
Korean Sentence 1: 저는 한 달에 다섯 번 이상 극장에 가니까 자주 가는 편이에요.
English Sentence 1: I go to the theater relatively often, considering that I go five times or more a month.
Korean Sentence 2: 코리 씨가 노래를 잘 못한다고요? 그 정도면 잘하는 편이에요.
English Sentence 2: You think Corey doesn't sing well? He sings relatively well.
Korean Sentence 3: 플릭 씨는 키가 큰 편이지요.
English Sentence 3: Flick is pretty tall.
Korean Sentence 4: 안느 씨, 한국 음식을 처음 만들었는데 이 정도면 맛있는 편이지요.
English Sentence 4: Anne, it's your first time making Korean food and this is pretty good.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 주디씨, 토미씨는 어떤 사람이에요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 말이 별로 없는 편이지만 같이 있으면 재미있어요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Judy, what kind of person is Tommy?
English Sentence 5B: B: He may seem relatively untalkative but he's fun to be around.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 날이 이렇게 더운데 집까지 30분이나 걸어가야 해요. 너무 멀어요.
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 그 정도면 가까운 편이지요. 저는 한 시간 이상 걸려요.
English Sentence 6A: A: It's so hot and I have to walk 30 minutes to get home. It's too far.
English Sentence 6B: B: That's pretty close. It takes me more than an hour to get home.

Explanation: To express that you were just about to do something.
Korean Sentence 1: 저도 지금 점심을 먹으려던 참이었어요.
English Sentence 1: I was just about to eat lunch, too.
Korean Sentence 2: 그렇지 않아도 네게 부탁하려던 참이었어.
English Sentence 2: As a matter of fact, I was just about to ask you.
Korean Sentence 3: 저도 커피를 마시려던 참이었어요. 같이 가요.
English Sentence 3: I was just about to drink coffee, too. Let's go together.
Korean Sentence 4: 그렇지 않아도 노라 씨한테 연락하려던 참이었어요.
English Sentence 4: As a matter of fact, I was just about to contact you, Nora.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 3시 기차를 타려면 지금 출발해야 될 것 같은데요.
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 그렇지 않아도 이제 출발하려던 참이었어요.
English Sentence 5A: A: I think we need to leave now in order to board the 3 o'clock train.
English Sentence 5B: B: As a matter of fact, I was just about to leave.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 에릭씨, 지금 통화할 수 있어요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 네, 유키씨, 저도 유키씨에게 전화하려던 참이었어요.
English Sentence 6A: A: Are you available to talk on the phone right now, Eric?
English Sentence 6B: B: Yes, Yuki. I was just about to call you.

Explanation: To indicate that someone "only" does that action and nothing else.
Korean Sentence 1: 제 친구는 책을 사기만 하고 읽지는 않아요.
English Sentence 1: My friend only buys books; she never reads them.
Korean Sentence 2: 아이가 밥도 안 먹고 울기만 해요.
English Sentence 2: The baby doesn't even eat and only cries.
Korean Sentence 3: 어제 잠을 못 자서 영화를 볼 때 계속 졸기만 했어요.
English Sentence 3: I didn't get much sleep last night, so I just kept falling asleep during the movie.
Korean Sentence 4: 주말에 저는 쉬지도 않고 공부만 했어요.
English Sentence 4: I had no time to rest; I only studied during the weekend.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 어머니께서 요리를 하실 때 마리아 씨도 같이 했어요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 아니요, 저는 옆에서 보기만 했어요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Did you help your mother with the cooking, Maria?
English Sentence 5B: B: No, I just watched from the side.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 일요일에 밀린 집안일을 좀 했어요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 아니요, 너무 피곤해서 쉬기만 했어요.
English Sentence 6A: A: Were you able to get some overdue chores done on Sunday?
English Sentence 6B: B: No, I was too tired so I just rested.

Explanation: To express that someone "must" or "should" do something.
Korean Sentence 1: 약속을 했으면 지켜야지요.
English Sentence 1: If you make a promise, you need to keep it.
Korean Sentence 2: 담배는 밖에 나가서 피워야지.
English Sentence 2: You need to smoke outside.
Korean Sentence 3: 2시까지 도착하려면 지금 출발해야지요.
English Sentence 3: You need to leave now if you want to arrive by 2 p.m.
Korean Sentence 4: 산에 올라갈 때는 불편한 신발을 신지 말아야지.
English Sentence 4: You can't wear uncomfortable shoes when climbing a mountain.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 영수 씨가 저에게만 한 이야기를 실수로 다른 사람에게 말했어요.
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 비밀 이야기는 다른 사람에게 말하지 말아야지요.
English Sentence 5A: A: I accidentally spilled the beans on the secret that Yeongsu only shared with me.
English Sentence 5B: B: You shouldn't tell others a secret (that's been told to you).
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 요즘 회사 일 때문에 잠을 못 자서 너무 피곤해.
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 일이 많아도 무리하지 말고 좀 쉬어야지.
English Sentence 6A: A: I'm so tired these days. I don't get much sleep because we're so busy at work.
English Sentence 6B: B: Even if you're busy, you shouldn't overdo it. You need to rest.

Explanation: Used with a descriptive verb to say someone/something "looks" a certain way.
Korean Sentence 1: 더러웠던 방을 청소하니까 방이 넓어 보여요.
English Sentence 1: The room looks bigger after I cleaned up the mess.
Korean Sentence 2: 흐엉 씨는 나이보다 어려 보여요.
English Sentence 2: Huong, you look younger than your age.
Korean Sentence 3: 요즘 일이 많아요? 피곤해 보여요.
English Sentence 3: Are you busy these days? You look tired.
Korean Sentence 4: 어제 친척 결혼식에 갔는데 신랑과 신부가 아주 행복해 보였어요.
English Sentence 4: I attended a relative's wedding yesterday and the bride and groom looked so happy.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 이 영화가 재미있어 보이는데 우리 이 영화를 볼까요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 좋아요. 저도 보고 싶었던 거예요.
English Sentence 5A: A: This movie looks fun. Do you want to watch it?
English Sentence 5B: B: Sure. I've been wanting to watch it, too.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 정말 예쁜 케이크네요. 맛있을 것 같아요.
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 네, 저도 맛있어 보여서 샀어요.
English Sentence 6A: A: It's a really pretty cake. I think it'll be tasty.
English Sentence 6B: B: Yes, I bought it because it looked tasty.

Explanation: To make a hypothetical supposition about something ("if... were to happen").
Korean Sentence 1: 마음에 드는 사람을 찾는다면 결혼할 거예요.
English Sentence 1: If I find someone I like, I'm going to marry him/her.
Korean Sentence 2: 만약 10억이 생긴다면 집을 사고 싶어요.
English Sentence 2: If I got a billion dollars, I would want to buy a house.
Korean Sentence 3: 시험이 없다면 정말 행복할 것 같아요.
English Sentence 3: If there were no tests, I think I would be so happy.
Korean Sentence 4: 내가 너라면 담배를 피우지 않겠어.
English Sentence 4: If I were you, I wouldn't smoke.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 뭐든지 만들 수 있다면 뭘 만들고 싶어요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 뭐든지 만들 수 있다면 젊어지는 약을 만들고 싶어요.
English Sentence 5A: A: If you could make anything, what would you want to make?
English Sentence 5B: B: If I could make anything, I would want to make a potion that makes people younger.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 과거로 돌아갈 수 있다면 언제로 돌아가고 싶어?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 유치원 때로 돌아가고 싶어. 그때는 친구만 있으면 행복했어.
English Sentence 6A: A: If you could go back in time, when would you want to return to?
English Sentence 6B: B: I want to return to kindergarten. Back then, all I needed was friends to be happy.

Explanation: To suggest a possible reason for something ("Perhaps it's because...").
Korean Sentence 1: 요즘 과로해서 그런지 자주 머리가 아파요.
English Sentence 1: Perhaps it's because I'm overworked these days, but my head frequently hurts.
Korean Sentence 2: 근처에 공원이 있어서 그런지 집값이 비싸요.
English Sentence 2: Perhaps it's because there's a park nearby, but the houses here are expensive.
Korean Sentence 3: 요즘 날씨가 더워서 그런지 입맛이 없어요.
English Sentence 3: Perhaps it's because it's so hot out these days, but I don't have an appetite.
Korean Sentence 4: 유명한 관광지여서 그런지 비가 와도 사람이 많군요.
English Sentence 4: Perhaps it's because it's a famous tourist attraction, but there are a lot of people even when it rains.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 존 씨는 참 똑똑한 것 같아요.
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 책을 많이 읽어서 그런지 아는 것이 많아요.
English Sentence 5A: A: I think John is very smart.
English Sentence 5B: B: Perhaps it's because he reads a lot, but he's well-informed.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 이 가방은 디자인은 예쁜데 너무 비싼 것 같아요.
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 너무 비싸서 그런지 사람들도 구경만 하고 안 사네요.
English Sentence 6A: A: The bag's design is very pretty, but I think it's too expensive.
English Sentence 6B: B: Perhaps it's because it's too expensive, but people just look and don't buy.

Explanation: The passive voice, where the subject is acted upon.
Korean Sentence 1: 올리비아 씨 집에서는 학교가 잘 보여요.
English Sentence 1: The school can be seen from Olivia's house.
Korean Sentence 2: 도둑이 경찰에게 잡혔어요.
English Sentence 2: The thieves were caught by the police.
Korean Sentence 3: 미라 씨와 통화하고 있었는데 갑자기 전화가 끊겼어요.
English Sentence 3: I was talking to Mira on the phone when the phone suddenly got cut off.
Korean Sentence 4: 핸드폰이 고장난 것 같아요. 버튼을 눌러도 켜지지 않아요.
English Sentence 4: I think the cell phone is broken. Even if I push the button, it isn't being turned on.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 제 이야기가 잘 들리세요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 잘 안 들려요. 좀 더 크게 말씀해 주세요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Can you hear me?
English Sentence 5B: B: Your voice can't be heard clearly. Please speak louder.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 미라야, 공책이 바뀌었어. 여기 이게 네 공책이야.
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 그래? 공책이 똑같아서 바뀐 줄 몰랐어.
English Sentence 6A: A: Mira, our notebooks were switched. Here's your notebook.
English Sentence 6B: B: Really? The notebooks are the same, so I didn't even know they were switched.

Explanation: To indicate the state that remains after an action has been completed.
Korean Sentence 1: 고양이 밥 그릇이 비어 있네요.
English Sentence 1: The cat's food bowl is empty.
Korean Sentence 2: 책상 위에 교과서가 놓여 있었어요.
English Sentence 2: The textbook was on the desk.
Korean Sentence 3: 가방에 무엇이 들어 있었어요?
English Sentence 3: What was in the bag?
Korean Sentence 4: 미선 씨 방에 불이 켜져 있네요.
English Sentence 4: The lights are on in Miseon's room.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 미라 씨, 집이 좀 추워요.
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 창문이 열려 있는데 닫을까요?
English Sentence 5A: A: Mira, your house is a bit cold.
English Sentence 5B: B: The windows are open. Should I close them?
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 윤아야, 내 모자가 어디에 있지?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 저기 옷걸이에 걸려 있어.
English Sentence 6A: A: Yuna, where's my hat?
English Sentence 6B: B: It's hanging on the coat rack over there.

Explanation: To express thoughts about choosing between options ("whether to... or...").
Korean Sentence 1: 저는 친구 결혼식 때 원피스를 입을지 바지를 입을지 생각 중이에요.
English Sentence 1: I'm still deciding whether to wear a dress or slacks to my friend's wedding.
Korean Sentence 2: 저는 기숙사에 살지 하숙집에 살지 아직 결정하지 못했어요.
English Sentence 2: I haven't decided yet whether to live in the dormitory or boarding house.
Korean Sentence 3: 이번 학기에 역사 수업을 들을지 문화 수업을 들을지 생각하고 있어요.
English Sentence 3: I'm still debating whether to take the history class or the culture class this semester.
Korean Sentence 4: 다음 방학 때 고향에 갈지 여행을 갈지 아직 잘 모르겠어요.
English Sentence 4: I'm not sure whether to visit my hometown or travel during the next vacation.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 링링 씨, 졸업 후에 뭘 할 거예요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 대학원에 갈지 일을 할지 아직 결정하지 못했어요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Ling Ling, what are you going to do after you graduate?
English Sentence 5B: B: I haven't decided yet whether to go to graduate school or get a job.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 마리아 씨, 여행을 가면 어디에서 잘 거예요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 호텔에서 잘지 친구 집에서 잘지 생각 중이에요.
English Sentence 6A: A: Maria, if you go on vacation, where do you plan to stay?
English Sentence 6B: B: I'm still debating whether to stay at a hotel or at my friend's house.

Explanation: To indicate an action is completed and its result is being maintained for later use.
Korean Sentence 1: 시원하게 마시려고 냉장고에 음료수를 넣어 놓았어요.
English Sentence 1: I've put the beverage in the refrigerator so I can drink it cold.
Korean Sentence 2: 내일 아침에는 시간이 없을 것 같아서 가방을 미리 싸 놓았어요.
English Sentence 2: I've packed my bags early since I don't think I'll have time tomorrow morning.
Korean Sentence 3: 휴가철에 여행을 가려면 미리 기차표를 예매해 놓아야 해요.
English Sentence 3: You have to buy your train ticket in advance in order to travel during the vacation season.
Korean Sentence 4: 이제 요리를 시작할 테니까 재료들을 꺼내 놓으세요.
English Sentence 4: Please have your ingredients out since we will begin cooking.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 내일이 노라 씨 생일인데 케이크는 준비했어요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 네, 제가 만들어 놓았어요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Tomorrow is Nora's birthday. Have you prepared the cake?
English Sentence 5B: B: Yes, I've baked it.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 저한테 전화 온 거 없어요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 책상 위를 보세요. 제가 메모해 놓았어요.
English Sentence 6A: A: Have there been any calls for me?
English Sentence 6B: B: Look on your desk. I've made memos of your calls.

Explanation: The shortened form for reported speech ("He/she said...").
Korean Sentence 1: 에릭 씨가 다음 달에 고향에 돌아간대요.
English Sentence 1: Eric says he's going to return to his hometown next month.
Korean Sentence 2: 고향 친구한테서 어제 전화가 왔는데 저에게 잘 지내고 있냬요.
English Sentence 2: I received a call from my hometown friend and he asked me if I'm doing well.
Korean Sentence 3: 윤아 씨가 내일 날씨가 추우니까 따뜻한 옷을 입고 오래요.
English Sentence 3: Yuna said to dress warmly tomorrow since it's going to be cold.
Korean Sentence 4: 친구가 주말에 시간이 있으면 같이 놀러 가재.
English Sentence 4: My friend said she wants to spend time with me on the weekend if I have time.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 유키 씨가 왜 아직 안 오지요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 아까 연락이 왔는데 조금 늦는대요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Why isn't Yuki here yet?
English Sentence 5B: B: She called a little while ago and said she was going to be a bit late.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 조금 전에 리타오가 뭐라고 했어?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 오늘 점심을 같이 먹재.
English Sentence 6A: A: What did Letao say a minute ago?
English Sentence 6B: B: He wants to eat lunch together today.

Explanation: Used with ~나/나 to mean "anyone," "anything," "anytime," etc.
Korean Sentence 1: 여기는 아무나 들어갈 수 있어요?
English Sentence 1: Can anyone come in here?
Korean Sentence 2: 이번 주는 한가하니까 아무 때나 연락하세요.
English Sentence 2: I'm not busy this week so you can call anytime.
Korean Sentence 3: 목이 마르니까 마실 것이 있으면 아무거나 주세요.
English Sentence 3: I'm so thirsty. If you have anything to drink, please give it to me.
Korean Sentence 4: 검은색 구두는 아무 옷에나 다 잘 어울려요.
English Sentence 4: Black shoes go well with any outfit.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 내일 파티에 무슨 옷을 입고 가야 돼요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 중요한 자리가 아니니까 아무 옷이나 입어도 돼요.
English Sentence 5A: A: What do I need to wear to tomorrow's party?
English Sentence 5B: B: It's not an important event, so just wear anything.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 오늘 한 귀걸이가 정말 예쁘다. 학교 앞에서 샀어?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 아니, 이건 디자이너가 직접 만든 거라서 아무데서나 팔지 않아.
English Sentence 6A: A: Your earrings today are really pretty. Did you buy them in front of the school?
English Sentence 6B: B: No, a designer hand made them, so they don't just sell them anywhere.

Explanation: To state a realization or outcome resulting from a past action.
Korean Sentence 1: 제가 오랜만에 고향에 갔더니 친구들이 모두 떠나고 없었어요.
English Sentence 1: Because I visited my hometown for the first time in a long time, all my friends had all left.
Korean Sentence 2: 오늘 아침에 음식을 급하게 먹었더니 소화가 잘 안 돼요.
English Sentence 2: Because I ate so quickly this morning, I'm having a hard time digesting the food.
Korean Sentence 3: 제가 노래를 불러 줬더니 여자친구가 행복해했어요.
English Sentence 3: My girlfriend was happy because I sang a song for her.
Korean Sentence 4: 제가 하늘 씨한테 물어봤더니 하늘 씨도 모른대요.
English Sentence 4: I asked Haneul, but he said he didn't know either.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 에릭 씨, 어디 아프세요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 며칠 과로했더니 병이 났어요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Eric, are you feeling sick?
English Sentence 5B: B: I got sick because I overworked myself for a few days.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 링링 씨, 이사할 때 도와줄 사람은 있어요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 네, 제가 다음 주말에 이사한다고 했더니 친구들이 도와주겠대요.
English Sentence 6A: A: Ling Ling, is anyone helping you during the move?
English Sentence 6B: B: Yes. I said that I was moving next weekend, so my friends said they would help me.

Explanation: To remind or confirm something the listener already knows ("As you know...").
Korean Sentence 1: 잊어버렸어요? 제가 아까 말했잖아요.
English Sentence 1: Have you forgotten? I told you earlier.
Korean Sentence 2: 레오 씨가 요리를 잘하잖아요.
English Sentence 2: (As you know) Leo is a good cook.
Korean Sentence 3: 우리 학교 시험이 좀 어렵잖아요.
English Sentence 3: (As you know) Our school's exams are a bit hard.
Korean Sentence 4: 내일부터 연휴잖아요.
English Sentence 4: (As you know) Starting tomorrow, we have consecutive holidays.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 걱정했는데 시험을 잘 봤어.
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 내가 걱정하지 말라고 했잖아.
English Sentence 5A: A: I was worried, but I did well on the exam.
English Sentence 5B: B: Didn't I say you had nothing to worry about?
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 왜 이렇게 열심히 공부해요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 다음 주에 시험이 있잖아요.
English Sentence 6A: A: Why are you studying so diligently?
English Sentence 6B: B: (As you know) There's a test next week.

Explanation: To indicate that one action happens "after" another is completed.
Korean Sentence 1: 저는 어제 영화를 보고 나서 늦게 저녁을 먹었어요.
English Sentence 1: After watching a movie yesterday, I ate a late dinner.
Korean Sentence 2: 미선 씨, 우리 밥 먹고 나서 커피를 마시러 학교 앞 커피숍에 갈까요?
English Sentence 2: Miseon, should we go to the coffee shop in front of the school to get a cup of coffee after we eat?
Korean Sentence 3: 저는 책을 읽고 나서 영화를 보니까 이해하기가 쉬웠어요.
English Sentence 3: It was easy for me to understand the story because I watched the movie after reading the book.
Korean Sentence 4: 노라가 가고 나서 올리비아가 왔어요.
English Sentence 4: Olivia arrived after Nora left.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 미즈키, 우리 영화부터 보고 나서 밥을 먹을까?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 나는 지금 배가 많이 고파. 먼저 밥부터 먹자.
English Sentence 5A: A: Mizuki, why don't we eat after watching the movie?
English Sentence 5B: B: I'm so hungry right now. Let's eat first.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 엄마, 저 한 시간만 게임해도 돼요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 숙제 먼저 다 하고 나서 게임해라.
English Sentence 6A: A: Mom, can I play games for just one hour?
English Sentence 6B: B: Play your game after you finish your homework.

Explanation: To ask for confirmation about something you heard ("Is it true that...?").
Korean Sentence 1: 요즘 이튼 씨 회사에서 드라마를 찍는다면서요?
English Sentence 1: Is it true that a drama series is being filmed at your company these days, Ethan?
Korean Sentence 2: 서울 타워에서 보이는 경치가 그렇게 멋있다면서요?
English Sentence 2: Is it true that the view from Seoul Tower is amazing?
Korean Sentence 3: 영화 '그날'에 나오는 남자 배우가 우리 학교 학생이라면서요?
English Sentence 3: Is it true that the actor who comes out in the movie "That Day" is a student from our school?
Korean Sentence 4: 미키 씨, 어렸을 때 한국에서 살았다면서요?
English Sentence 4: Miki, is it true that you lived in Korea when you were younger?
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 우리 학교에 '남자친구들'이 공연하러 온다면서요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 네, 저도 아까 들었어요. 정말 기대가 돼요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Is it true that "Boyfriends" is coming to perform at our school?
English Sentence 5B: B: Yes, I heard that, too. I'm so excited.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 왕명 씨, 이번 방학에 고향에 간다면서요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 네, 어떻게 아셨어요?
English Sentence 6A: A: Wang Ming, is it true that you're going to visit your hometown during the break?
English Sentence 6B: B: Yes, how did you know?

Explanation: To express "even though" or "despite" something.
Korean Sentence 1: 저는 날마다 운동을 하는데도 건강이 별로 좋아지지 않아요.
English Sentence 1: Even though I exercise every day, my health is not improving.
Korean Sentence 2: 날씨가 추운데도 공원에 운동하는 사람들이 많아요.
English Sentence 2: Although the weather is cold, there are a lot of people exercising in the park.
Korean Sentence 3: 평일인데도 극장에 사람들이 많았어요.
English Sentence 3: There were a lot of people at the theater, even though it was a weekday.
Korean Sentence 4: 저는 주말에 푹 쉬었는데도 감기가 낫지 않아서 병원에 갔다 왔어요.
English Sentence 4: Even though I rested all weekend, my cold didn't get better so I went to the hospital.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 영수 씨, 요즘도 테니스 연습을 열심히 하고 있어요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 네, 하지만 날마다 연습을 하는데도 실력이 늘지 않아요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Yeongsu, do you still practice tennis diligently these days?
English Sentence 5B: B: Yes, but even though I practice every day, my skills don't improve.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 오늘은 날씨가 정말 춥지요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 네, 두꺼운 코트를 입고 있는데도 추워서 몸이 떨려요.
English Sentence 6A: A: It's really cold today, isn't it?
English Sentence 6B: B: Yes. Even though I'm wearing a thick coat, it's still cold so I'm shivering.

Explanation: Attached to a verb to mean "it is easy to..."
Korean Sentence 1: 계절이 바뀌는 때에는 감기에 걸리기가 쉬워요.
English Sentence 1: It's easy to catch a cold when the seasons change.
Korean Sentence 2: 유리 제품은 깨지기가 쉬워요.
English Sentence 2: Glass products are easily broken.
Korean Sentence 3: 틀리기가 쉬운 문제를 공책에 써 놓았어요.
English Sentence 3: I wrote down the test questions that are easy to get wrong in my notebook.
Korean Sentence 4: 비가 온 후라서 뛰면 넘어지기가 쉽겠어요. 천천히 갑시다.
English Sentence 4: It seems like it would be easy to slip and fall since it just rained, so let's take our time.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 요즘 회사 일 때문에 너무 바빠서 동창회 날짜를 잊어버렸어.
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 바빠서 기억을 못했구나. 잊어버리기가 쉬운 날짜는 메모해 놓는 게 좋아.
English Sentence 5A: A: I've been so busy at work lately that I forgot the date of our reunion.
English Sentence 5B: B: Oh I see. You forgot because you were so busy. You should write down dates that are easy to forget.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 주말이라서 그런지 사람도 많고 길이 정말 복잡하네요.
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 너무 복잡해서 길을 잃기가 쉽겠어요. 지도를 보면서 갑시다.
English Sentence 6A: A: Perhaps it's because it's the weekend, but there are a lot of people and the streets are really crowded.
English Sentence 6B: B: It seems like it'll be easy to get lost because it's so complicated. Let's look at the map and find our way there.

Explanation: To express uncertainty or possibility ("might" or "may").
Korean Sentence 1: 날씨가 추운데 친구가 밖에서 기다릴지도 몰라서 서둘러서 나왔어요.
English Sentence 1: I rushed just in case my friend might be waiting outside in the cold.
Korean Sentence 2: 오늘은 늦을지도 모르니까 기다리지 마세요.
English Sentence 2: Don't wait up, I might be late today.
Korean Sentence 3: 그 공연은 인기가 많아서 늦게 가면 자리가 없을지도 몰라요.
English Sentence 3: That performance is so popular that if we go late, there may not be any seats left.
Korean Sentence 4: 신청 기간이 끝났을지도 모르니까 다시 확인해 보세요.
English Sentence 4: The registration period may be over, so you should check again.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 올리비아 씨가 계속 전화를 안 받아요.
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 자고 있을지도 몰라요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Olivia isn't picking up her phone.
English Sentence 5B: B: She might be sleeping.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 지금 학교에 가면 선생님을 만날 수 있을까?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 안 계실지도 모르니까 먼저 연락을 드려 보자.
English Sentence 6A: A: If I go to school now, can I meet with the teacher?
English Sentence 6B: B: She may not be there, so give her a call first.

Explanation: Used with verbs of change to plan for a future point in time ("In order for it to be...").
Korean Sentence 1: 밥이 다 되려면 10분 남았다.
English Sentence 1: There are 10 minutes left until the rice is ready.
Korean Sentence 2: 이나무에 꽃이 피려면 아직 멀었어요.
English Sentence 2: It's too soon for the flowers on these trees to bud.
Korean Sentence 3: 집에 도착하려면 지금부터 1시간은 더 가야 돼요.
English Sentence 3: We need to go an hour from now to arrive at home.
Korean Sentence 4: 다친 팔이 다 나으려면 앞으로 2주 더 치료를 받아야 한다.
English Sentence 4: In order for your arm to heal completely, you'll need to be treated two more weeks.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 회의 전에 잠깐 감기약을 사러 약국에 가고 싶은데 시간이 될까?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 회의가 시작되려면 30분 정도 더 있어야 하니까 빨리 갔다 와.
English Sentence 5A: A: I want to stop by the pharmacist to pick up some cold medication before the meeting. Do you think I'll be able to make it?
English Sentence 5B: B: You should hurry up since the meeting will start in about 30 minutes.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 저기요, 저희가 주문한 음식은 언제 나오나요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 죄송합니다. 오늘 손님이 많아서 음식이 나오려면 좀 더 기다리셔야 합니다.
English Sentence 6A: A: Excuse me, when will our food be ready?
English Sentence 6B: B: I'm sorry. We have a lot of customers today, so you'll have to wait a little longer for your food to come out.

Explanation: Used when listing examples ("... or something like that").
Korean Sentence 1: 비빔밥이라든가 삼계탕 같은 한국 음식이 건강에 좋아요.
English Sentence 1: Korean foods like bibimbap or samgyetang are good for the health.
Korean Sentence 2: 아이들은 초콜릿이라든가 사탕 같은 단 맛이 나는 것을 좋아해요.
English Sentence 2: Children like sweets like chocolate or candy.
Korean Sentence 3: 테니스라든가 배드민턴 같은 공을 가지고 하는 운동을 해보세요.
English Sentence 3: Try a sport you can play with a ball like tennis or badminton.
Korean Sentence 4: 주말이라든가 공휴일 같은 쉬는 날에는 보통 가족들과 시간을 보내요.
English Sentence 4: I usually spend days that I have off like weekends or holidays with my family.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 일요일 오후에는 보통 뭘 하세요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 빨래라든가 청소 같은 집안일을 해요.
English Sentence 5A: A: What do you usually do on Sunday afternoon?
English Sentence 5B: B: I usually do household chores like the laundry or cleaning.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 요즘 일 때문에 너무 스트레스를 받아요.
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 노래방이라든가 놀이공원 같은 스트레스를 풀 수 있는 곳에 가는 게 어때요?
English Sentence 6A: A: These days, I have so much stress from work.
English Sentence 6B: B: Why don't you try going to places that can help you relieve stress like noraebangs or amusement parks?

Explanation: To make a speculation about a past event ("must have," "probably").
Korean Sentence 1: 지금 3시니까 영화가 끝났을 거예요.
English Sentence 1: It's 3 p.m, so the movie is probably over already.
Korean Sentence 2: 봉봉 케이크는 인기가 많아서 벌써 다 팔렸을 거예요.
English Sentence 2: That type of cake is really popular. It's probably already all sold out.
Korean Sentence 3: 나오 씨는 오늘 저녁에 친구와 약속이 있다고 했어요. 아마 식사를 했을 거예요.
English Sentence 3: Nao said she had an appointment with a friend tonight. I'm sure she already ate.
Korean Sentence 4: 우진 씨가 도와주지 않았으면 에릭 씨 혼자 정말 힘들었을 거예요.
English Sentence 4: It would have been so hard for Eric on his own if Woojin hadn't helped out.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 메리 씨가 소포를 받았겠지요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 보통 미국까지 나흘 정도 걸리잖아요. 아직 못 받았을 거예요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Mary probably received the package, right?
English Sentence 5B: B: It usually takes four days for a delivery to be made to the U.S. I don't think she received it yet.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 윤아 씨가 집에 도착했을까요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 출발한 지 한 시간이나 지났으니까 집에 도착했을 거예요.
English Sentence 6A: A: Do you think Yuna arrived at home?
English Sentence 6B: B: It's been an hour since she left. I'm sure she arrived at home.

Explanation: To make an assumption based on visual evidence ("It looks like...", "I guess...").
Korean Sentence 1: 노라 씨에게 연락했는데 전화를 안 받아요. 벌써 자나 봐요.
English Sentence 1: I called Nora, but she wouldn't pick up. Maybe she's already sleeping.
Korean Sentence 2: 주앙 씨가 오늘도 학교에 안 왔어요. 많이 아픈가 봐요.
English Sentence 2: Juang didn't come to school again today. He must be really sick.
Korean Sentence 3: 유키 씨 옆에 있는 여자가 유키 씨와 똑같이 생겼어요. 동생인가 봐요.
English Sentence 3: The woman next to Yuki looks exactly like her. She must be her sister.
Korean Sentence 4: 벌써 그 많은 음식을 다 먹었어? 정말 배가 고팠나 보네.
English Sentence 4: You've already finished all that food? You must have been very hungry.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 식당 앞에 사람들이 길게 줄을 서 있어요.
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 이 식당 음식이 정말 맛있나 봐요.
English Sentence 5A: A: There's a long line in front of that restaurant.
English Sentence 5B: B: The food there must be really delicious.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 저 두 사람에게 무슨 일이 있었어?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 하루 종일 서로 말을 안 해. 싸웠나 봐.
English Sentence 6A: A: Did something happen between them?
English Sentence 6B: B: They haven't spoken to each other all day. They must have had an argument.

Explanation: To formally state one's opinion ("I think that...").
Korean Sentence 1: 저는 리에 씨가 잘못했으니까 리에 씨가 먼저 사과해야 한다고 생각해요.
English Sentence 1: I think that Rie needs to apologize first because she's the one who made the mistake.
Korean Sentence 2: 나는 기차로 가는 것보다 버스로 가는 게 더 낫다고 생각하는데 어때?
English Sentence 2: I think it's better to go by bus than train. What do you think?
Korean Sentence 3: 회사를 선택할 때 제일 중요한 것은 회사의 분위기라고 생각합니다.
English Sentence 3: I think that the company culture is most important when choosing which company to work for.
Korean Sentence 4: 나는 제임스가 거짓말을 했다고 생각해.
English Sentence 4: I think James was lying.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 열심히 공부하는데도 한국어 실력이 늘지 않아서 걱정이야.
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 혼자 공부하는 것도 좋지만 한국 사람들과 많이 이야기하는 게 중요하다고 생각해.
English Sentence 5A: A: I'm worried because my Korean isn't improving, even though I'm studying hard.
English Sentence 5B: B: I think it's good to study alone, but it's more important that you talk to a lot of Korean people.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 중학생이 화장을 하는 것은 나이에 맞지 않기 때문에 하면 안 된다고 생각합니다.
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 저는 화장을 하면 안 되는 나이는 없다고 생각합니다.
English Sentence 6A: A: I don't think it's appropriate for middle school students to wear make-up because it's not fit for their age.
English Sentence 6B: B: I don't think there's a set age you need to be in order to wear make-up.

Explanation: To indicate doing one thing "instead of" another, or "in return for" something.
Korean Sentence 1: 주변이 시끄러워서 전화를 하는 대신에 문자 메시지를 보냈어요.
English Sentence 1: It was so noisy that instead of making a phone call, I sent a text message.
Korean Sentence 2: 시간이 없어서 극장에 가는 대신에 집에서 영화를 봤어요.
English Sentence 2: I didn't have time, so instead of going to the theater, I watched a movie at home.
Korean Sentence 3: 미선 씨가 제 일을 도와주는 대신에 저는 미선 씨에게 저녁을 사 드릴게요.
English Sentence 3: In return for you helping me with my work, Miseon, I'll buy you dinner.
Korean Sentence 4: 오늘 우진 씨가 바빠서 우진 씨 대신에 제가 왔어요.
English Sentence 4: Woojin is busy today so I came here today instead of him.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 우진 씨, 일요일에도 출근하세요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 네, 하지만 일요일에 일하는 대신에 월요일에는 쉽니다.
English Sentence 5A: A: Woojin, do you go to work on Sundays, too?
English Sentence 5B: B: Yes, but in return for working on Sundays, I get Mondays off.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 우리 언어 교환을 할까요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 좋아요, 리에 씨가 저에게 일본말을 가르쳐 주는 대신에 저는 리에 씨에게 한국말을 가르쳐 드릴게요.
English Sentence 6A: A: Should we do a language exchange?
English Sentence 6B: B: Sounds good. In return for you teaching me Japanese, Rie, I'll teach you Korean.

Explanation: The causative form, meaning "to make/let someone do something."
Korean Sentence 1: 친구가 저를 화나게 했어요.
English Sentence 1: My friend made me angry.
Korean Sentence 2: 어렸을 때 어머니가 식사 전에 꼭 손을 씻게 하셨어요.
English Sentence 2: When I was younger, my mom always made me wash my hands before meals.
Korean Sentence 3: 아이들이 밖에 나가서 놀게 해 주세요.
English Sentence 3: Let the children play outside, please.
Korean Sentence 4: 우리 회사는 건물 안에서 담배를 피우지 못하게 합니다.
English Sentence 4: Our company doesn't let employees smoke inside the building.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 손님, 기다리게 해서 죄송합니다.
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 괜찮아요. 별로 오래 안 기다렸어요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Sir, I'm sorry for making you wait.
English Sentence 5B: B: No problem. I haven't been waiting that long.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 우리 아이가 게을러서 걱정이에요.
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 아이가 스스로 방을 청소하게 하세요. 그럼 부지런해질 거예요.
English Sentence 6A: A: I'm worried because my child is so lazy.
English Sentence 6B: B: Make him clean his own room. Then, he will become more industrious.

Explanation: To express a contrast between two actions or states by the same subject ("even while...").
Korean Sentence 1: 미아 씨는 노래를 잘하면서도 못한다고 해요.
English Sentence 1: Mia is good at singing, but she says she isn't.
Korean Sentence 2: 저는 과식이 건강에 안 좋은 줄 알면서도 항상 많이 먹어요.
English Sentence 2: I know that overeating is bad for the health, but I always eat a lot.
Korean Sentence 3: 이 옷은 가벼우면서도 따뜻해서 추울 때 자주 입어요.
English Sentence 3: I often wear this in the winter because it's light but warm.
Korean Sentence 4: 노라 씨는 다이어트 중이라서 밥을 안 먹었으면서도 먹었다고 말했어요.
English Sentence 4: Nora is dieting, so she said she had eaten when in fact, she hadn't.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 노라 씨, 언니하고 또 싸웠어요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 싸우면 안 되는 줄 알면서도 화가 나서 참지 못했어요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Nora, did you fight with your sister again?
English Sentence 5B: B: I know I shouldn't, but I just can't keep my anger in.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 패티 씨가 이번 시험에서 92점을 받았다면서요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 네, 그런데 패티 씨는 시험을 잘 봤으면서도 못 봤다고 하네요.
English Sentence 6A: A: I heard Patty got a 92 on her test.
English Sentence 6B: B: Yes, but even though she did well, she says she didn't.

Explanation: To provide background information based on personal experience before giving advice, making a suggestion, or asking a question.
Korean Sentence 1: 미선 씨, 민주 백화점에서 세일을 하던데 같이 갈래요?
English Sentence 1: Miseon, I saw Minju Department Store is having a sale. Would you like to go?
Korean Sentence 2: 주말에는 놀이공원에 사람이 많던데 평일에 가세요.
English Sentence 2: There are a lot of people at the amusement park on the weekends, so you should go on a weekday.
Korean Sentence 3: 교회 앞에 식당이 새로 생겼던데 오늘은 거기에 가자.
English Sentence 3: I saw there's a new restaurant in front of the church, so let's go there today.
Korean Sentence 4: 또와 치킨이 참 맛있던데 노라 씨도 먹어 봤어요?
English Sentence 4: Ddowa Chicken is so delicious. Have you eaten there, Nora?
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 설악산에는 등산하기가 좀 힘들던데 가보셨어요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 아니요, 아직 설악산에는 안 가 봤어요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Seoraksan is hard to climb. Have you been there?
English Sentence 5B: B: No, I haven't been to Seoraksan yet.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 오랜만에 친구를 보기로 했는데 어디에서 만나면 좋을까?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 지하철 역 앞에 커피숍이 새로 생겼던데 거기에 가 봐.
English Sentence 6A: A: I decided to see my friend for the first time in a long time. Where should I meet him?
English Sentence 6B: B: There's a new coffee shop in front of the subway station. Give it a try.

Explanation: To indicate a sequence of actions, emphasizing the first action is done before the second ("and then").
Korean Sentence 1: 카드를 넣고서 비밀번호를 누르세요.
English Sentence 1: Put in your card and then input your PIN.
Korean Sentence 2: 저는 컴퓨터를 켜고서 필요한 정보를 검색했어요.
English Sentence 2: I turned on the computer and searched for the necessary information.
Korean Sentence 3: 어제 저는 친구들과 빨간색 옷을 입고서 축구 경기를 보러 갔어요.
English Sentence 3: My friends and I dressed in red yesterday and went to watch the soccer game.
Korean Sentence 4: 저는 친구가 하는 이야기를 듣고서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
English Sentence 4: I was surprised upon hearing my friend's story.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 마리아 씨는 지금 뭘 해요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 대학원을 졸업하고서 한국 회사에 들어갔대요.
English Sentence 5A: A: What is Maria doing now?
English Sentence 5B: B: She graduated from graduate school and joined a Korean company.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 미선 씨, 왜 그래요? 발이 아파요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 네, 어제 구두를 신고서 오래 걸었더니 발이 아파요.
English Sentence 6A: A: Miseon, what's the matter? Does your foot hurt?
English Sentence 6B: B: Yes, I wore heels and walked for a long time yesterday, so my foot hurts.

Explanation: To express that something almost happened ("nearly," "almost").
Korean Sentence 1: 길이 막혀서 약속 시간에 늦을 뻔했어요.
English Sentence 1: There was so much traffic that I was almost late to my appointment.
Korean Sentence 2: 조금만 늦게 도착했으면 비행기를 못 탈 뻔했어요.
English Sentence 2: If I had arrived just a little later, I would have missed my plane.
Korean Sentence 3: 오늘 중요한 회의가 있었는데 동료에게 연락을 안 했으면 큰일 날 뻔했어요.
English Sentence 3: There was an important meeting today and we would have been in big trouble if I hadn't called my colleague.
Korean Sentence 4: 옆 사람과 이야기하면서 운전하다가 사고가 날 뻔했어요.
English Sentence 4: I almost got into a car accident talking to the passenger while driving.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 웨이 씨가 사고가 나서 병원에 입원했다면서요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 네, 조금만 늦게 병원에 갔으면 큰일 날 뻔했대요.
English Sentence 5A: A: I heard that Wei got into an accident and is in the hospital.
English Sentence 5B: B: Yes, they say that if she had arrived at the hospital a few minutes late, it would have been dangerous.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 오늘 회의에 필요한 서류를 다 챙겼어요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 아, 고마워요. 이야기해 주지 않았으면 서류를 놓고 갈 뻔했네요.
English Sentence 6A: A: Do you have all the documents for the meeting today?
English Sentence 6B: B: Oh, thanks. If you hadn't reminded me, I would have left them.

Explanation: The causative form, where the subject makes someone else perform an action.
Korean Sentence 1: 올리비아 씨가 차를 마시려고 물을 끓였어요.
English Sentence 1: Olivia boiled the water to drink tea.
Korean Sentence 2: 할머니가 아이를 침대에 눕혔어요.
English Sentence 2: The grandma laid the child on the bed.
Korean Sentence 3: 레오 씨, 이 정보를 많은 사람들에게 알려 주세요.
English Sentence 3: Leo, you should make more people know this information.
Korean Sentence 4: 저는 세탁소에 맡긴 옷을 찾으러 가야 해요.
English Sentence 4: I need to go and pick up the clothes I dropped off at the dry cleaners.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 내일 아침에 일찍 일어나야 한다고 했지?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 네, 혹시 제가 못 일어나면 깨워 주세요.
English Sentence 5A: A: You said you need to wake up early in the morning tomorrow, right?
English Sentence 5B: B: Yes. If I don't wake up, please wake me up.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 내일 오전 10시에 회의가 있다고 들었는데 맞아요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 과장님께서 오전에 해야 할 일이 있다고 하셔서 회의 시간을 2시로 늦췄어요.
English Sentence 6A: A: I heard that there's a meeting at 10 a.m. tomorrow. Is this true?
English Sentence 6B: B: The Director said there's something he needs to take care of in the morning, so he delayed the meeting to 2 o'clock.

Explanation: To state that the second clause was discovered or realized as a result of the action in the first clause.
Korean Sentence 1: 떡볶이를 먹어 보니까 생각보다 안 매웠어요.
English Sentence 1: After eating tteokbokki, I realized it wasn't as spicy as I had thought it would be.
Korean Sentence 2: 냉장고를 여니까 아무것도 없었어요.
English Sentence 2: I opened the refrigerator to discover that there was nothing inside.
Korean Sentence 3: 인터넷으로 주문한 옷을 입어 보니까 옷이 작았어요.
English Sentence 3: I tried on the clothes I ordered online only to find that they were too small.
Korean Sentence 4: 아침에 일어나니까 10시였어요.
English Sentence 4: I woke up in the morning to find that it was 10 a.m.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 한국 생활이 어때요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 혼자 살아 보니까 생각보다 재미있어요.
English Sentence 5A: A: How is life in Korea?
English Sentence 5B: B: After living alone, I've realized it's more fun than I had expected.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 어제 친구가 소개해 준 사람은 잘 만났어요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 네, 만나 보니까 좋은 사람이었어요.
English Sentence 6A: A: Did you meet the person your friend set you up with yesterday?
English Sentence 6B: B: Yes, and he was a good person.

Explanation: To express that something contrary to one's intention happened ("I was trying to... but...").
Korean Sentence 1: 커피에 설탕을 넣는다는 것이 소금을 넣었어요.
English Sentence 1: I was trying to put sugar in my coffee but happened to put salt in.
Korean Sentence 2: 시청으로 가는 지하철을 탄다는 것이 다른 쪽으로 가는 지하철을 탔어요.
English Sentence 2: I was trying to get on the subway train headed to City Hall but happened to go in the opposite direction.
Korean Sentence 3: 친구에게 전화한다는 것이 깜빡 잊고 못했어요.
English Sentence 3: I planned to call my friend, but forgot and couldn't.
Korean Sentence 4: 도와 드린다는 것이 일을 더 힘들게 만든 것 같아요.
English Sentence 4: I was trying to help, but I feel like I only made matters worse.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 소희야, 이게 누구 옷이니?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 어머, 제 옷을 챙긴다는 것이 미나 옷을 가지고 왔나 봐요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Sohee, whose clothes are these?
English Sentence 5B: B: Oh my. I was planning on bringing my clothes but brought Mina's clothes instead.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 도와 준다는 것이 일을 더 복잡하게 만든 것 같아요.
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 그런 말씀 마세요. 정말 큰 도움이 됐어요.
English Sentence 6A: A: I was only trying to help, but I think I ended up complicating matters.
English Sentence 6B: B: Don't say that. You were a great help.

Explanation: To express that something ended up happening, often regrettably or unintentionally ("ended up V-ing").
Korean Sentence 1: 화가 나도 참아야 하는데 그만 화를 내고 말았어요.
English Sentence 1: I should have kept in my anger, but I happened to get angry.
Korean Sentence 2: 정희 씨는 너무 졸려서 씻지도 못하고 잠이 들고 말았어요.
English Sentence 2: Jeonghee was so tired that she fell asleep without even washing up.
Korean Sentence 3: 민수 씨는 공항에 늦게 도착해서 비행기를 못 타고 말았어요.
English Sentence 3: Minsu arrived late at the airport and couldn't get on the plane.
Korean Sentence 4: 의사가 최선을 다했지만 환자는 죽고 말았어요.
English Sentence 4: The doctor did the best she could, but the patient ended up dying.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 노라 씨가 왜 저렇게 화가 났어요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 제가 친구들과 이야기하다가 실수로 노라 씨의 비밀을 말하고 말았어요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Why is Nora so angry?
English Sentence 5B: B: I was talking with my friends and happened to share Nora's secret.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 아까 왜 시험 시간에 늦었어요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 어제 너무 늦게 자서 아침에 늦잠을 자고 말았어요.
English Sentence 6A: A: Why were you late to the test earlier?
English Sentence 6B: B: I slept late last night and overslept this morning.

Explanation: Used at the end of a sentence to provide a reason or explanation for a previous statement.
Korean Sentence 1: 누리 씨는 학교에서 인기가 많아요. 노래를 아주 잘하거든요.
English Sentence 1: Nuri is very popular at school because she is a good singer.
Korean Sentence 2: 저는 보통 대한마트에서 쇼핑을 해요. 물건값이 싸거든요.
English Sentence 2: I usually shop at Daehan Mart because the products are cheaper there.
Korean Sentence 3: 오늘은 정말 쉬고 싶어요. 몸살 감기가 심하거든요.
English Sentence 3: I really just want to rest today because I have a terrible cold and body aches.
Korean Sentence 4: 이번 주말에는 못 만나요. 친구들과 놀이공원에 가기로 했거든요.
English Sentence 4: I can't make it this weekend because I'm going to the amusement park with my friend.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 케빈 씨, 무슨 일이 있어요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 여자친구가 화가 많이 났어요. 제가 약속을 어겼거든요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Is something the matter, Kevin?
English Sentence 5B: B: My girlfriend is really mad because I broke a promise.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 미선 씨, 오늘 아주 피곤해 보여요. 어디 아파요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 어제 2시간밖에 못 잤거든요. 빨리 집에 가서 쉬고 싶어요.
English Sentence 6A: A: Miseon, you look so tired today. Are you feeling unwell?
English Sentence 6B: B: It's because I only slept two hours last night. I want to quickly go home and get some rest.

Explanation: To express worry or concern that something might happen ("I'm afraid that...").
Korean Sentence 1: 비가 올까 봐 우산을 가지고 왔어요.
English Sentence 1: Just in case it rains, I brought an umbrella.
Korean Sentence 2: 지각할까 봐 택시를 타고 왔어요.
English Sentence 2: I was afraid I would be late, so I took a cab.
Korean Sentence 3: 친구들이 놀릴까 봐 말하지 않았어요.
English Sentence 3: I was afraid my friends would make fun of me, so I didn't say anything.
Korean Sentence 4: 버스가 출발했을까 봐 걱정했어요.
English Sentence 4: I was worried that the bus would leave.
Korean Sentence 5A: 가: 줄리 씨, 왜 이렇게 일찍 왔어요?
Korean Sentence 5B: 나: 길이 막힐까 봐 오늘은 집에서 일찍 출발했어요.
English Sentence 5A: A: Why did you come so early, Julie?
English Sentence 5B: B: I was afraid there would be traffic, so I left early from home today.
Korean Sentence 6A: 가: 은하 씨, 왜 그렇게 천천히 걸어가세요?
Korean Sentence 6B: 나: 넘어질까 봐 조심하는 거예요.
English Sentence 6A: A: Eunha, why are you walking so slowly?
English Sentence 6B: B: I'm afraid I might fall, so I'm being careful.
